Patterns that match byte-identical baseline NFTStaker code (e.g. REWARD-ACCRUAL-ORDER, REWARD-RUNWAY-DEPLETION, EMISSION-WINDOW-BOUNDARY, BATCH-PAYOUT-FIXED-POT) were intentionally skipped per request because they do not intersect the delta. The profile establishes the solvency ledger (balance == rewardBudget + committedDebt) is structurally insensitive to priceScale, so those host-file patterns carry no new delta-driven risk.

manualReview.patternName: Token-Decimal Normalization / Wrong Scaling Factor (custom; not in DB v1.0)
manualReview.description: The entire reason this contract exists is decimal normalization: `latestPrice = latestPrice * priceScale` lifts a prime-token-decimal mint price (e.g. 6dp USDC, priceScale=1e12) into 18dp phUSD reward units so the emission rate is decimal-correct. The constructor validates `_priceScale != 0` only (L230) and CANNOT verify decimal-consistency (it has no view of prime/reward token decimals). A wrong priceScale (e.g. 1e6 vs 1e12, or 1 left over from an 18dp-priced clone retargeted at a 6dp dispatcher) silently mis-sizes the per-second emission rate by orders of magnitude in EITHER direction: too-large over-emits (faster budget drain / higher effective APY than intended), too-small under-emits (stakers paid far below targetAPY). This is precisely the decimal-mismatch failure class the contract was built to fix — applied with the wrong constant it reintroduces it. Direction note: priceScale is the MULTIPLY-UP factor (10**(rewardDecimals - priceDecimals)); inverting the direction (treating it as a divide-down) is the classic wrong-direction scaling bug, here structurally impossible (it is a bare multiply) but a wrong MAGNITUDE is fully possible.
matchedSignatures: require(_priceScale != 0, ...) (line 230) -- non-zero only, no decimal-consistency check
missingMitigations: No on-chain decimal-consistency assertion (priceScale == 10**(rewardDecimals - priceDecimals)); contract cannot read prime-token decimals
Immutable: a wrong value cannot be corrected post-deploy -- requires redeploy
manualReview.lawAnalysis: Set once at deploy, immutable, instantly observable on-chain -> a wrong value is a Law-3 owner config-correctness boundary, NOT a contract-local exploit. Borderline footgun: the SURPRISE test (CLAUDE.md Law 3) is plausibly met because the correct value (10**(rewardDecimals - priceDecimals)) is non-obvious and silently mis-sizes emissions rather than reverting -- a competent non-malicious owner could be surprised. Routed to manual review for a human/econ-scanner to adjudicate whether the missing decimal-consistency guard rises to a reportable operational hazard (Low/QA footgun) or stays a documented trust assumption. Confidence is LOW about whether the pattern yields a reportable FINDING, not about the decimal mechanics, which are certain.

manualReview.patternName: Hand-Maintained Mirror Silently Diverges / Omits a Fix (custom; not in DB v1.0)
manualReview.description: NFTStakerPriceScaled is, by its own NatSpec (L32-38), a hand-maintained standalone COPY of NFTStaker whose ONLY intended deltas are the contract name, the priceScale immutable + its guard, and the single multiply at L435. Everything else is asserted mirror-identical but is NOT enforced by inheritance, a shared base, or a compile-time check. This is the classic fork-drift hazard: the audited NFTStaker carries fixes M-01 (strip committedDebt from V before budgeting, L447-453) and M-03 (size rate against staked subset S = totalStaked * latestPrice, L437-440). If a future fix lands on NFTStaker and the maintainer forgets to mirror it here (or vice versa), this copy silently diverges and one variant ships an un-fixed bug. The risk is structural/process, not a present-state local bug: at HEAD eee9d3a the M-01 and M-03 fixes ARE present in this copy (verified in profile). The reportable angle is the absence of a drift guard (shared base contract or invariant test asserting byte-equivalence of the non-delta region).
matchedSignatures: NatSpec L32-38 declaring this a copy of NFTStaker with enumerated deltas
M-01 fix mirrored at L447-453 (budget = V > committedDebt ? V - committedDebt : 0)
M-03 fix mirrored at L437-440 (S = totalStaked * latestPrice)
missingMitigations: No shared abstract base / inheritance from NFTStaker -- the two are independent files
No cross-file equivalence test asserting the non-delta region stays in sync
Divergence is silent (compiles clean either way)
manualReview.lawAnalysis: Law 1 recall: must not be silently dropped even though no present-state bug exists -- a future un-mirrored fix is a plausible security regression vector. Routed to manual review (and worth a story-faithfulness / process note) rather than a code finding because the current copy is faithful. Confidence LOW on whether this yields a reportable finding vs a QA/process recommendation.

manualReview.description: Floor-rounding division-before-multiply intersecting the delta: `latestPrice = price.mulDiv(APY_PRECISION, r)` (L430) floors FIRST, then `latestPrice = latestPrice * priceScale` (L435) multiplies. The priceScale multiply AMPLIFIES the up-to-1-wei floor truncation by the scale factor: with priceScale=1e12, the worst-case absolute lost magnitude on latestPrice grows from <1 wei to <1e12 wei. The floor happens on the price BEFORE scaling, so the dropped sub-wei fraction of the unscaled price is multiplied up. This is the textbook precision-loss-then-amplification shape (floor before multiply). However the RELATIVE error stays ~1e-21 (latestPrice is ~1e33 after scaling; the amplified absolute error ~1e12 is ~21 orders of magnitude smaller), and the direction is conservative-for-protocol (floor under-promises the rate). No exploit; the amplification is real but economically negligible at intended scales. Would only matter if priceScale were absurdly large (itself an obvious misconfig, Law 3).
matchedSignatures: latestPrice = latestPrice * priceScale (L435, amplifying multiply AFTER the floor)
missingMitigations: Floor truncation is taken before the priceScale multiply (amplifies the dropped fraction)
manualReview.lawAnalysis: The amplified error is conservative-for-protocol (floor under-promises) and economically negligible (~1e-21 relative). Not a Law-1 exploit; not a Law-2 story break (NatSpec L413-419 explicitly mandates floor and forbids ceiling). Informational. Reorder note: multiplying by priceScale BEFORE the mulDiv (i.e. price.mulDiv(APY_PRECISION*priceScale, r) or scaling the numerator) would eliminate the amplification, but the current order is safe-direction so the change is cosmetic, not required.

manualReview.patternName: Immutable Set Without Bounds at Deploy (custom; not in DB v1.0)
manualReview.description: `priceScale` is `public immutable` (L94), set once in the constructor (L236) behind only `require(_priceScale != 0)` (L230). No upper bound and no semantic validation. Because it is immutable, ANY error -- wrong magnitude (see PS-001), or an absurd value that pushes L435 (latestPrice*priceScale) or L440 (totalStaked*latestPrice) into a checked-arithmetic revert -- can only be remedied by redeploying the contract and re-migrating stakers. An absurd value (>~1e40 combined with large price/supply) bricks _recomputeSchedule via overflow-revert, which would DoS stake/unstake/topUp/setTargetAPY (all call recompute); emergencyWithdraw still escapes principal (it never reads priceScale, L577-600). The DoS is a checked revert, not silent wraparound, and an absurd immutable is an obvious deploy-time misconfig.
missingMitigations: No upper bound on _priceScale at construction
Overflow on absurd value is a recompute DoS (mitigated for principal by emergencyWithdraw)
manualReview.lawAnalysis: An absurd priceScale is an OBVIOUS owner misconfig observable at deploy (Law 3 -> trusted/suppress for the overflow-DoS angle). The non-obvious magnitude error overlaps PS-001 and is routed there. Listed here for completeness of the immutable-misconfig family; on its own the overflow-DoS angle is suppressed-leaning (obvious + principal escapes). Confidence LOW.

manualReview.patternName: Reward-Emission Rate Manipulation / Budget Drain (delta-intersection check)
manualReview.description: Delta-intersection of the reward-emission/budget-drain family: priceScale linearly scales latestPrice -> S -> F -> rewardRate (L435->L440->L455->L456). A priceScale set too LARGE inflates rewardRate, draining the funded reward budget faster than intended (over-emission / shorter runway than the operator believes). This is a rate MIS-SIZING via the immutable scale, NOT a manipulation vector: priceScale is immutable and owner-set, not user/attacker-influenceable, and the solvency clamp still holds (windowEnd shortens as rate rises, _updatePool clamps reward to rewardBudget, _safePay reverts on shortfall) so the protocol never pays MORE than it holds -- it just pays out the held budget faster / over the wrong APY. No insolvency, no double-mint, no attacker path. Collapses into the decimal-correctness footgun PS-001 (same root cause: wrong scale -> wrong rate). Recorded separately to show the budget-drain pattern was checked against the delta and resolves to a config footgun, not an exploit.
matchedSignatures: rewardRate, rewardBudget, windowEnd, committedDebt (host-file emission state)
latestPrice = latestPrice * priceScale propagating into newRate = F / SECONDS_PER_YEAR
missingMitigations: No effect: solvency invariant (balance == rewardBudget + committedDebt) and the min(now, windowEnd) clamp bound actual payout regardless of rate (profile invariants #1, #3)
manualReview.lawAnalysis: Not a Law-1 exploit (no attacker-influenceable input; solvency holds). Maps onto the same owner config-correctness boundary as PS-001 (over-emission is the too-large half of the wrong-magnitude footgun). Routed to manual review folded with PS-001; no independent finding.
